Employment of population individuals in the labour market lives in contracts; the population's exogenous `employer` column and `employed` feature do not see it (CORE-POP migration, facts.py KNOWN_DUPLICATES pop.employer). The economy reads both through economy.popbridge.employment; other packages still see only the exogenous column.
Employer demand for labour comes only from incumbents' support queues (rivals staffing rule); industry, science and education employers do not recruit from the population yet.
Mutual-aid associations insure job loss only; their thresholds (FR-WORK-3) are uncalibrated.

Display campaigns: attention is the reference value 1 per displayed period (work.display_attention); the in-world holdout therefore checks the mechanism, not attention; the incremental conversion ratio is not applied.
Passes are 30-day term licences of services; goods and content listings by population sellers are not modelled.

gov proposals in worlds with inst are inst decisions: 4.0 society minds (actors.negotiation) read the gov proposals table and therefore no longer vote on them there (no in-world caller of gov.propose exists in civilisations).

Earlier limitations of F+G (wave 2) that remain: source-of-funds tracing replays the ledger; platform review filters look one hop back; work.value and rivals rules uncalibrated; labour task quality formula (labor.task_quality) unchanged; subjective usefulness (6.3) not implemented.

The population buys, disputes and rates on exchanges but does not sell there: nothing an individual produces is a listable product (services need a deployed program, documents and goods have no population production path in commerce); the population sells its labour through the labour market instead.
Labour demand follows incumbents' support backlog: in saturated startup worlds employment can fall to the founders alone for a week or more before new tickets bring hiring back.

Short civilisation runs (<= 5 days) have no hire yet: the labour market's employers in a civilisation are the incumbents (support backlog, from day 3) until I-2's firms/plantlabor are composed, so employment is active (registrations) but not connected in Gate O's 5-day window on this branch.

Mutual-aid claims (FR-WORK-3): a claim that qualifies under the published terms but that no voter can check (the claimant is not a contact and has no labour-market record) gets the benefit of the doubt (yes 0.6), so an agent that never had a job can still draw at most one benefit per claim gap (365 days) after 30 days of membership and dues in two months - bounded (the verifier's probe drained 8 benefits, 48x its dues; now <= 1 a year), not eliminated: members have no other evidence of a job (the population's exogenous employer is not a public record).

Working time (labor.working_time): labor.shift is capped per worker at 12 h a calendar day and the worker's contracted hours_week (<= 48) per calendar week, shifts do not overlap; simulated workers' hours come from the 4.0 worker model (hours_week / 7 a day times an effort factor <= 1.15) and are not bounded by it; an agent's shift hours are not charged to its in-world time budget. Overtime, paid leave and part-time multi-job limits across labour markets are not modelled.
